synthesis.paragraph: "How built environment factors shape demand for demand-responsive transport services: spatiotemporal patterns from a German case study" shares seven references with the July 9 paper "Rural microtransit service to replace fixed route service: A California case study", including "Investigating the contribution of Demand Responsive Transport to a sustainable local public transport system", "Exploring the propensity to travel by demand responsive transport in the rural area of Lincolnshire in England", and "The actual demand behind demand-responsive transport: Assessing behavioral intention to use DRT systems in two rural areas in Germany". This same German case study paper also shares three references with the July 10 paper "Optimizing demand-responsive feeder transit stop locations for transportation hubs: A multi-objective approach", including "Why most DRT/Micro-Transits fail – What the survivors tell us about progress", "Built environment as a precondition for demand-responsive transit (DRT) system survival: Evidence from an empirical study", and "How successful is my DRT system? A review of different parameters to consider when developing flexible public transport systems". Additionally, "COSMOLOGICAL MARKINGS AND ERASURES: The Political Theology of State‐Led Gentrification and Heritagization" shares four references with the June 28 paper "ALL POSSIBLE PASTS: Heritage, Simulacra, and Gentrification in Seoul", with shared works including "Heritage Production and Urban Locational Policy in Lijiang, China", "Uses of Heritage", and "HERITAGIZATION AS AN AUTHORITARIAN URBAN PRACTICE IN CHINA: Insights from Lijiang". Finally, Hong Kong Polytechnic University appears on two of today's papers, and has appeared on 28 papers in the last 30 days, while Tongji University, Peking University, and Beijing Jiaotong University have appeared on 30, 19, and 17 papers respectively over the same 30-day period.
